# Intentional divergences from the Python implementation

One line per divergence: area | case | python behavior | go behavior | reason.
The goldens still pin Python's observable output; entries here are changes no
scenario can see (or, after the cutover, golden updates recorded with
`-impl=go -update`).

- telemetry | `telemetry enable|disable` on a config whose last line is a bare `telemetry:` anchor without a trailing newline | the inserted child is glued onto the anchor (`telemetry:  enabled: true`), invalid YAML | the anchor line is ended first (`telemetry:\n  enabled: true\n`) | real bug; no conformance scenario covers it, so the goldens are unchanged
- telemetry | `record` with an integer field above int64 (e.g. `usage.input_tokens: 99999999999999999999`) | stored as a bignum | the field is dropped by the sanitizer | token counts never approach 2^63; dropping keeps the allowlist guarantee
- sandbox | concurrent `sandbox allow` / `allow-domain` / `forget*` and auto grants | unlocked read-modify-write loses entries | updated under an exclusive lock (`sandbox-learned.json.lock`, 10 s timeout); store byte format unchanged | lost grants are a real bug
- check | a check whose shell cannot be started (e.g. `cwd` names a missing directory) | uncaught FileNotFoundError traceback, exit 1 | the check is reported as `fail` (exit null) with the start error as its output excerpt | a crash in the middle of a run lost every other result; no conformance scenario covers it
- wave lint | plan.json that is not valid JSON | `invalid JSON in plan <path>: <Python JSONDecodeError text>` | same prefix, Go's decoder text after it | the decoder wording cannot be reproduced; the scenario compares the prefix only
- wave lint | plan.json with a malformed shape the Python loader did not validate (`packages` not a list, a non-object package entry, non-string `files_owned`/`depends_on`/`preamble`/`external_done` items) | uncaught AttributeError/TypeError traceback | `plan.Error` with a message, exit 3 | a lint tool should say what is wrong; no conformance scenario covers it
- check | JUnit failure `message` attribute containing a raw newline/tab (not `&#10;`) | ElementTree normalizes it to a space, so the header keeps the whole message on one line | encoding/xml keeps the raw newline, so the header shows only the first line | low impact on the fixer excerpt; correct normalization needs raw-attribute scanning
- integrate | `--verify` command that exits while a background child still holds its output pipe | waits on the pipe until `--verify-timeout`, then reports a timeout | stops collecting output 5s after the command exits and grades its exit status | a daemonized child must not turn a finished verify into an hour-long hang
- integrate | the lock file under `.git/orchestra/` cannot be created | uncaught OSError (traceback, exit 1) | `status: error` with the reason in `note`, exit 3 | a repository failure belongs in the result, not a crash
- adopt | `isolate adopt --task` with no usable characters (e.g. `//`) | uncaught ValueError (traceback, exit 1) | usage error, exit 2, like every other isolate subcommand | real bug; no conformance scenario covers it
- adopt | `isolate adopt --baseline ""` | error "could not resolve --baseline ref ''" (exit 3) | treated as no `--baseline` (the tree's HEAD) | the domain API takes "" as "not given"; an empty ref is never meaningful
- watchdog | `watchdog.repeat_limit` that is not a number (or a bool, or <= 0) | a string/None crashes the watchdog thread (no budget enforced at all); 0 trips `repeat` at the first check | the repeat check is off, every other budget still applies | a typo must not silently disable the wall/idle budgets
- watchdog | `idle_seconds` / `tool_idle_seconds` / a `wall_seconds` entry that is not a number | the watchdog thread dies on the comparison (no budget enforced) | the value is ignored and its default applies | same reason
- pi | a JSONL line holding the non-standard literals `NaN` / `Infinity` | parsed by json.loads | not JSON: the line is unparseable and goes to the availability scan | pi never emits them; encoding/json rejects them
- capture | child stdout/stderr bytes that are a truncated multi-byte UTF-8 sequence | one U+FFFD per maximal invalid subpart | one U+FFFD per invalid byte | only invalid UTF-8 differs; valid output is identical
- capture | `_merge_usage` across grant cycles | merged keys in set (hash) order, varying between runs | the first run's keys, then the resumed run's new keys | deterministic; key order is outside the contract
- tools | the managed pi agent dir cannot be created | OSError propagates and the dispatch crashes | PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR still names it and pi reports the failure | a dispatch result beats a traceback
- dispatch | `run <profile> ...` | the direct executor run | removed; `dispatch --executor pi --model M --effort E --workdir W --prompt-file F [--class] [--run-id] [--resume] [--isolate] [--task]` prints the same bare capture result (isolate default `never`; an `isolation` key only when another mode is asked for; no session store) | owner decision; the `dispatch/direct` goldens are captured from `run pi --capture` and replayed through `argv_go`
- dispatch | `dispatch session` | read-only session-store CLI | removed (the store itself is unchanged) | owner decision
- dispatch | direct-mode usage | (no such mode) | `--executor` with `--archetype`/`--exhausted`/`--no-cooldown`/`--no-resume` is "dispatch: --executor conflicts with ...", `--model`/`--effort` without it "dispatch: --model requires --executor", an executor without a CLI profile "dispatch: unknown executor: X"; `--token` also conflicts with `--executor`/`--model`/`--effort` | new flags need defined errors
- dispatch | `--task ""` (or a token whose task is "") | an empty task id: isolation fails with "could not isolate (task id '' ...)" and the session store is keyed by it | the same as no `--task` | the domain request uses "" for "not given"
- dispatch | the detached child | `shutil.which("agent-exec")` (else the Python script) | `os.Executable()` re-run as `dispatch <args>` in a new session | owner decision; the detach files have the same format, so a run detached by one implementation is waited on by the other (mixed scenarios)
- dispatch | the detached child cannot be started | uncaught exception (traceback) | `{"status": "relay-failed", "token", "raw": "could not start the detached dispatch: ..."}` | the relay protocol already treats relay-failed as a failed hop
- dispatch | detach state file | `json.dumps` with ASCII escapes, written in place | non-ASCII kept, written atomically | same decoded content; a reader never sees a torn state
- dispatch | `dispatch wait` with a result file that is JSON but not an object | printed as the result | treated as no result yet | only `dispatch` itself writes that file, always an object
- dispatch | two `dispatch wait` collecting the same finished, uncollected child at once | one removes `<T>.out` before the other reads it, and the loser overwrites `<T>.result.json` with relay-failed | the collect step holds an exclusive flock on `detach/<T>.lock` (30 s, then best effort unlocked); the loser re-reads and returns the collected result | real race; the lock file is new, every other detach file is unchanged
- dispatch | `ListDetached` (agent-exec ui) | `os.listdir` order | sorted by token | deterministic
- dispatch | retention sweep | one process-wide flag shared by the ledger append and the dispatch sweep | `dispatch.SweepRetention` (ledger + tokens + sessions + detach files) has its own once-per-process guard; `ledger.Append` still sweeps the ledger dir | an extra ledger-dir pass at most; nothing is kept longer
- write-file | stdin that is not UTF-8 | UnicodeDecodeError traceback, exit 1 | "agent-exec: write-file: failed to write <path>: stdin is not valid UTF-8", exit 2 | a crash is not a diagnostic
- write-file | a parent path component is a file | uncaught makedirs error (traceback, exit 1) | "write-file: failed to write <path>: <error>", exit 2, like every other write failure | consistent error path
- write-file | `--expect-chars` beyond the int range | a bignum, always a mismatch (exit 1) | "--expect-chars must be an integer", exit 2 | no real count reaches it
- fakepi | `FAKEPI-HANG` | (Go fakepi) a bare `select {}` the runtime aborted as a deadlock (exit 2) | blocks until signalled | the directive is documented as "block until killed"; no golden used it
- host | `herdr.args` / `orca.command` that shlex cannot split (an unclosed quote) | uncaught ValueError from shlex.split (the package thread dies) | `error` need "invalid herdr.args: ..." / "invalid orca.command: ..." | a config typo should stop one package with a reason, not crash the runner
- host | `--plugin-dir` of the hosted Claude's isolation flags | the plugin root is the parent of the Python tools dir | the grandparent of `$AGENT_EXEC_BOOTSTRAP` (tools/agent-exec), else the nearest ancestor of the binary holding `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`; omitted when neither is found | the cached Go binary does not live in the plugin tree
- host | need details quoting a fractional timeout (`herdr X timed out after 120.0s`, `no result after 90.5s`) | Python's `%s` of a float (`120.0`) | integral seconds print without `.0` (`120`) | message text only; no scenario pins it
- host | a host wait interrupted by the runner (context cancelled) | not possible (threads are not cancelled) | the wait ends with an `error` need carrying the context error | the Go runner can stop in-flight packages
- host | screen tails in need details | `str.splitlines()` (also splits on \v, \f, \x1c-\x1e, \x85, U+2028/2029) | splits on \n, \r\n and \r only | terminal screens carry no other separators; display text only
- doctor | the `uv` block | `uv: {present: bool}` (text: `uv: present` / `uv: NOT found`) | `build: {binary, source_hash, go}` (text: `build: binary=... source_hash=... go=...`); `source_hash` is the bootstrap's cache directory name, else the binary's VCS revision, else null | the Go build needs no uv; the doctor scenarios carry `go_swap` (harness: the golden's key is dropped and Go's `build` object is checked for exactly those keys; volatile values are not compared)
- doctor | `config.warnings` | legacy/unknown-executor/codex-removed/pre-0.4 warnings; text `WARNING:` lines | always `[]`, no text lines | the legacy compatibility layer was removed; the scenarios avoid configs that warn
- doctor | `config.error` for an unparsable layer | PyYAML's multi-line message | Go yaml's one-line message after the same `agent-exec: invalid YAML in <path>: ` prefix | parser wording; `doctor/config-error` masks the `error` key (json) and uses `go_replace` (text)
- doctor | a layer whose top level is not a mapping (e.g. a list) | uncaught AttributeError traceback in `_scrub_codex` (exit 1) | `resolved: false` with `the top level must be a mapping`, exit 0 | real bug; no scenario covers it
- doctor | `cooldowns.active` entry | the stored dict as is | only `reason` and `until` | agent-exec writes nothing else
- doctor | the pi login probe (`login`, `hint`) | `agent_exec_pilogin.PiLogin.auth_ready` | `tools.PiAuthReady` / `tools.ConfiguredProviders` (internal/tools/pilogin.go), the one implementation `pi login` shares with the doctor | same output
- install | final line | `Quick test: agent-exec list` | `Quick test: agent-exec doctor` | `list` was removed; the install scenarios carry `go_replace`
- install | the bootstrap | the running Python file's directory, or a marketplace clone | a marketplace clone first (as before), else `$AGENT_EXEC_BOOTSTRAP` (also used in place of the Python file path to prefer the same marketplace among several clones); neither: `cannot locate the agent-exec bootstrap`, exit 1 | the cached Go binary does not live in the plugin tree
- install | a shim directory that cannot be created or a shim file that cannot be written | uncaught OSError traceback, exit 1 | `agent-exec: install: cannot create|write ...`, exit 1 | a message beats a traceback; stdout is identical and the scenarios do not compare stderr
- ui | the usage panel | `_usage_snapshot` walked the report's own top-level keys (`cost`, `scope`, `sources`, `totals`) as if they were executors, so the panel never held real numbers | `usage.Snapshot24h`: `{"<source>/<model>": {input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens[, cost_micro_usd]}}`, cached 60 s in the ui as Python's cache was | Python bug; `TestSnapshotMatchesPython` compares every other slot
- ui | the dispatch panel | reads files lying directly in the ledger dir as well as the per-session directories | per-session directories only (the flat layout was retired with `ledger.Paths`) | same as every other ledger reader
- ui | a state file that fails to parse (`waves[].error`) and a failing config (`error` slots) | the Python exception text | the Go error text | wording only; both are `{"error": ...}` in the same slot
- ui | POST `/api/cooldown/clear` with an unreadable config, POST `/api/sweep` that fails | an uncaught exception in the handler thread (the connection is dropped with no response) | HTTP 500 `{"error": ...}` | a reply beats a dropped connection
- ui | the server process | `python agent_exec_ui.py --serve` with cwd = the tools directory | the agent-exec binary itself (`ui --serve`) with cwd `/`, so no project config layer of whoever started it applies | there is no tools directory to run from; Python's cwd was equally unrelated to the caller's project
- ui | `--port` | only meaningful with the hidden `--serve`; a plain `ui --port N` ignored it | the same | kept; `StartOrReuse` takes a port for its callers
- ui | the conformance scenarios | n/a | `ui --json` start / reuse / `--stop` and the usage errors are scenarios; `/api/snapshot` is not (the harness cannot make HTTP calls), so `internal/ui` `TestSnapshotMatchesPython` starts the Python and the Go server on one fixture HOME and diffs the documents (skipped without uv; delete it with the Python implementation) | harness limit
- pi login | screen parsing | `str.splitlines()` and Unicode `\s` in the highlight regex | splits on \n, \r\n, \r; ASCII `\s` | terminal screens carry no other separators; the scenarios and `screen_test.go` pin the cases that matter
- wave run | the dispatch child | `sys.executable agent_exec.py dispatch ...` | the running binary (`os.Executable()`) re-run as `dispatch prepare` / `dispatch --token ... --detach` / `dispatch wait` | owner decision (plan §1); the token/detach files are shared, so `wave-run/mixed-*` resume one implementation's wave with the other
- wave run | gated self-verify | `cmd_check` run in-process with sys.stdout swapped for a per-thread buffer | `check` run in-process into a buffer through `runner.Deps.Check` (no stdout swapping; a child `agent-exec check` when no hook is set) | goroutines need no stdout routing; output and exit codes are the same
- wave run | the dashboard | `agent_exec_ui.start_or_reuse()` unless `--no-ui` / `ORCHESTRA_WAVE_NO_UI=1` | started through the `cli.WaveUIStart` seam, which is nil (no `ui:` line, no `ui` event) until the ui package wires it | the ui package lands separately; the scenarios run with `ORCHESTRA_WAVE_NO_UI=1` either way
- wave run | need details quoting a dispatch result's numbers (`exit_code` in a dispatch-error detail, `port` in network denials) | the dispatch JSON's int/float kept as decoded | integral numbers re-encoded as integers (`1.0` would print `1`) | the result is decoded with encoding/json; agent-exec only ever prints integers there
- wave run | an unexpected failure inside a package job | `runner error: <Python exception class>: <message>` | `runner error: RuntimeError: ...` (prepare failed), `OSError: ...` (a prompt file could not be written), `Error: ...` (anything else) | Go has no exception classes; the need kind and the prefix are unchanged
- wave run | an `await` job whose interactive session vanished before it ran | AttributeError on None, a `runner error` dispatch-error need | a `delegate` need with `orca: stalled`, `agent is no longer registered` | the package can be awaited again instead of re-dispatched
- wave run | `--notify-cmd` at the end of a run | each notify thread joined with a 35 s timeout | every notify command waited for (each is killed after 30 s) | same bound in practice
- wave run | `--into` with no usable characters (e.g. `///`) | uncaught ValueError traceback, exit 1 | an error report (`kind: environment`), exit 3 | a crash is not a report
- approvals | a `network_denials` entry that is not an object | AttributeError traceback | the entry is skipped | a hand-edited state file should not break the listing
